result.title: Deep Learning for Satellite-Based Mountain Hazard Screening: A Retrospective Failure Analysis on the 2021 Chamoli Rock-Ice Avalanche
result.summary: The approach utilizes 10 bands from Sentinel-2 imagery, along with terrain information, in a deep learning pipeline to classify potential hazard sources in any given mountainous region. The performance of our model has been evaluated against the data collected during the rock-ice avalanche event in the Chamoli region in the Indian Himalayas on 7th February 2021. U-Net performs segmentation of the detected land surface in the satellite image, detects changes in the identify candidate hazard zones, and then the following steps are performed to calculate the potential energy using the Monte Carlo sampling for steepest descent (D8) flow paths, finding the exposed structures in the downstream locations, and ranking the zones depending on the risk score. In comparison to the simple spectral rule, our approach achieved the higher macro F1 score of 0.648 (as compared to 0.519). But the F1 score in case of rock and soil was low, being in the range of 0.3s. In case of optical change detection in winter, it's only that northeast-facing slope which couldn't be detected, as it was under 73% of shade prior to the incident. The parameters have been set for this particular scene alone and not independently; hence, this is a retrospective test, and this test locates a failure which has occurred earlier. The primary contribution of this paper is locating the pipeline leak.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文用 Sentinel-2 多波段与地形数据构建 U-Net 分割、变化检测和 Monte Carlo 流路风险评估的遥感流程，对 2021 年 Chamoli 岩冰雪崩事件做回溯性失败分析，定位流程中的薄弱环节。
AI.relevance_reason: 属遥感灾害筛查任务，论述集中于光谱规则对比、阴影遮挡导致的检测失败与风险排序，没有涉及 VLM 内部推理状态、latent 证据使用或计算/停止决策，也未提供可核查的方法迁移线索，故排除。
